title: Validation Disc drawing-mode transition flash
symptom: When advancing between certain Drawing validation frames, a very brief lightning-like transition is visible. It occurs across every tested drawing representation, while each resulting still frame remains stable and does not shimmer.
expected: The shared drawing-mode transition is treated as authored validation-program behavior unless hardware evidence later shows otherwise; it is not conflated with the stationary artifact unique to CLUT 4 High Res.
revalidation_reason: Manual comparison found the same brief flash in every tested drawing mode, including modes whose stable output is clean. It is therefore closed as shared likely-authored transition behavior rather than evidence for the CLUT 4 High Res still-frame defect. Real-hardware evidence could justify reopening it.

scenario.dvc: vmpega present but unused by this base-graphics test
input_events: select CLUT 4, CLUT 4 High Res, CLUT 7, CLUT 8, or RGB
click repeatedly to advance between drawing modes

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The flash is most likely an authored transition or authored non-atomic drawmap update because it occurs across all tested drawing representations, including modes with clean stable output. The stable destination frame argues against a persistent weave defect.
supporting_evidence: The effect appears only briefly while changing modes.
The user's visual impression during the flash is of alternating field content.
The destination still frame does not alternate or shimmer.
The validation program exercises UCM drawing and display operations that may intentionally reveal update order.
The flash occurs in all tested modes rather than only CLUT 4 High Res.
contradicting_evidence: No high-frame-rate capture or consecutive field hashes exist yet.
No real-hardware capture independently proves that the authored transition should be visible exactly this way.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Record consecutive raw odd/even plane hashes and composed rasters from immediately before the click until the destination frame stabilizes, while also tracing DCA/display-file and UCM drawmap changes. If the guest intentionally supplies the transient fields, classify it as authored; if guest data is stable but composition alternates incorrectly, isolate the first divergent MCD212 or frontend stage.
citations: Philips Validation Disc Europe Disc 1, Visual Examples > Drawing
MCD212 Technical Specification, display-file switching and field timing
Green Book Release 2, UCM drawmap display operations

manual_verification.notes: A brief lightning-like animation appears between certain clicked drawing modes. It seems to expose alternating fields, but the resulting still is stable and non-shimmering.

The flash occurs in every tested drawing mode. Only CLUT 4 High Res has stationary line artifacts, so the shared transition is not being treated as part of that defect. Reopen only if hardware evidence contradicts this classification.
